# `m.indicators.macd`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

The moving average convergence/divergence of a ticker's bars, one row per bar.

```python
m.indicators.macd(symbols, *, short_window=12, long_window=26, signal_window=9, timespan=dm.Timespan.DAY, series_type=dm.SeriesType.CLOSE, adjusted=True, start=None, end=None, order=None, limit=None, filters=None)
```

| `filters` | none |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From REST: the request's `stockTicker` parameter; REST: the request's `cryptoTicker` parameter. | REST |
| `Date` | String | The trading day of the bar, as ISO yyyy-MM-dd text: the date of `TimestampStart` in the day zone of the symbol's class (UTC for forex and crypto, New York otherwise) for an intraday or 1-day bar, and null for a bar that spans more than one date (several days, a week or longer, or an intraday bar that crosses midnight). Joining an intraday row to the same day's daily bar on `Date` attaches values not known until that day ended, and a null `Date` matches another null, so join longer bars on `TimestampEnd`. | REST |
| `TimestampStart` | Instant | The start of the bar the value is computed at, as an Instant. A bar of a day or longer starts at 00:00 of its window's first day in the day zone of the symbol's class (UTC for forex and crypto, New York otherwise). A bar of a day or longer stamped at a time or on a day Massive is not known to use keeps that stamp, has a null `Date`, and ends one period after it, with a WARNING, since which day it covers is not known. From REST `timestamp`: "The Unix Msec timestamp from the last aggregate used in this calculation." | REST |
| `TimestampEnd` | Instant | The exclusive end of the bar's window, as an Instant: the first instant at which the bar is complete, so an as-of join on it, `t.aj(bars, on=["Symbol", "Timestamp>=TimestampEnd"])`, never attaches a bar that is still open. It is when the window closes, not when Massive published the bar, and Massive may correct a bar later. An intraday bar ends its length after its start; a bar of a day or longer at 00:00, in the day zone of the symbol's class, after its window's last day. A row read before its window ended has `TimestampInsert` before `TimestampEnd`, and its values can still change; `t.where("TimestampEnd <= TimestampInsert")` keeps only the rows read after their window ended. That test reads the local clock, which can be off, and a row read within moments of its end, or from a delayed feed, may still lack the window's last trades; an end set later than the window's (an index day's extra hour, a stamp kept as sent) only keeps a finished row out longer. | REST |
| `Value` | double | The MACD line value, calculated as the difference between the short-term and long-term exponential moving averages (EMAs) based on the periods specified in the request parameters. | REST |
| `Histogram` | double | The difference between the MACD line (value) and the signal line (signal). Positive histogram values indicate upward (bullish) momentum, while negative histogram values indicate downward (bearish) momentum. | REST |
| `Signal` | double | The signal line value, calculated as the exponential moving average (EMA) of the MACD line (value) over the signal period defined in the request parameters. Traders typically use crossovers between the MACD and signal lines as trading signals. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |
